issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: The car slips out of gear, loses gears, shifts late or harshly, or will not move forward. Many failures happen around 100,000-140,000 miles.
issues.why: The CD4E automatic in the Contour has a known weakness, often starting with the front pump. Ford also issued bulletins for no forward drive and no overdrive on this transmission.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. If it slips or will not move, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis. On a car this age a used or rebuilt transmission is usually the most sensible fix.

issues.t: Water pump failure and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant leaking from the front of the engine, the temperature gauge climbing, steam, or the engine overheating. Some owners replaced the pump several times.
issues.why: The water pump on these cars used a plastic impeller that can crack or break apart, and pump bearings and housings also failed. Ford sent owner notices about water pump bearing and housing failures.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as the gauge climbs, since overheating can ruin the head gasket. When replacing the pump, ask for one with a metal impeller.

issues.t: Stalls or dies while driving from fuel pump failure
issues.sym: The engine loses power and dies while driving, may restart after sitting, or cranks but will not start.
issues.why: Owners most often trace this to a failing fuel pump or no power reaching the pump. A tripped or faulty fuel shutoff (inertia) switch can do the same thing.
issues.next: If it dies, get safely off the road. Have a shop check fuel pressure and whether the pump is getting power before replacing parts.

issues.t: Blower motor resistor can overheat and melt (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell, some fan speeds stop working, or the blower quits. The connector may be melted.
issues.why: The heater blower resistor could overheat and damage its wiring connector, causing arcing and a fire risk. Ford recalled these cars to replace the resistor and harness and also extended the warranty on earlier cars.
issues.next: Stop using the fan if you smell burning. Check your VIN for the recall and have the resistor and connector replaced.

issues.t: Rear brakes can lock up from a corroded valve (recall)
issues.sym: The rear wheels lock or skid during hard braking, especially on cars driven on salted roads.
issues.why: On cars without ABS, the rear brake pressure-reducing valves could corrode from road salt and stop working, letting the rear brakes lock. Ford recalled 1996-1998 cars and later added 1999-2000 cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and make sure the improved valves were installed.

issues.t: Front coil springs can break and cut a tire (recall)
issues.sym: A loud clunk from the front, the car sitting lower on one side, or a front tire suddenly going flat.
issues.why: Front coil springs on Kansas City-built 1998 Contours sold in salt-belt states could rust and break, and a broken spring can rub through the tire. Ford installed spring catcher brackets and extended spring coverage.
issues.next: Look for a broken spring if you hear a front clunk. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Airbag sensor wiring can crack and disable airbags (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on and stays on.
issues.why: Heat from the radiator and water in the wiring sleeve made the airbag sensor wiring brittle. Cracked insulation can turn off the airbag system. Ford recalled these cars for new sensors and wiring.
issues.next: Have the airbag light checked. The airbags may not deploy while it is on.

issues.t: Headlights can go out from an overheated switch (recall)
issues.sym: The headlights or other lights flicker or suddenly go out, and the switch area may get hot.
issues.why: Headlight switch terminals and the wiring connector could overheat and burn, cutting power to the lights. Ford recalled these cars to install a better connector and inspect or replace the switch.
issues.next: If the lights flicker or go out, have the switch and connector checked right away.

issues.t: Accelerator cable can stick (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks or the engine idles high, so the car keeps accelerating or will not slow down normally.
issues.why: A burr inside the accelerator cable could make it bind. Ford recalled these cars for a revised cable.
issues.next: If the pedal sticks, shift to Neutral, brake, and pull over. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Throttle cable can fray on traction control cars (recall)
issues.sym: The engine does not return to idle when you lift off the gas.
issues.why: On 1996 Contours with traction control, throttle cables damaged at the factory could fray or separate. Ford recalled these cars for new cables.
issues.next: If the engine does not return to idle, shift to Neutral, brake and stop safely. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Shifter gear indicator damaged by cleaners (recall)
issues.sym: The P-R-N-D gear indicator on the shifter becomes hard to read or wrong, so you might pick the wrong gear.
issues.why: Some interior cleaners could damage the shifter and its gear indicator. Ford recalled these cars to replace the shift control.
issues.next: Always confirm the gear on the dash before letting off the brake. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Key can be removed when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can take the key out while the automatic transmission is not in Park, so the car could roll away.
issues.why: A fault in the steering column on some 1999 automatic Contours let the key come out outside of Park. Ford recalled these cars to inspect and replace the column where needed.
issues.next: Always check that the car is in Park and set the parking brake. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle may not latch securely (recall)
issues.sym: A seat belt that does not stay latched or releases under force.
issues.why: Some seat belt buckle bases on 2000 Contours were not heat treated correctly and could be weak. Ford recalled these cars to replace the buckles.
issues.next: Test that each belt latches firmly. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Radiator fan motor can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot electrical smell from the engine bay, the fan not running, or the engine running hot in traffic.
issues.why: The cooling fan motor bearings could overheat and create a fire risk. Ford added a protection device to the fan and extended its warranty on affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the fan is not running or you smell burning, have it checked before driving in traffic.

issues.t: Fuel filler vent hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the rear of the car, especially after filling up.
issues.why: The vent hose for the fuel filler could crack and leak fuel. Ford recalled these cars for a hose made from the correct material.
issues.next: Do not ignore a fuel smell. Check your VIN for the recall and have the hose inspected.

issues.t: Check engine light from clogged EGR passages
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an EGR flow code, and the engine may ping or knock under load.
issues.why: Carbon can plug the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) passages so not enough exhaust flows back into the engine. Ford issued a bulletin for EGR flow codes on these cars.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning the EGR passages and checking the EGR valve and sensor usually fixes it.

issues.t: Lean codes from vacuum leaks (V6)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes P0171 and P0174, and the idle may be rough.
issues.why: Cracked vacuum hoses or leaking intake gaskets let in extra air, making the engine run lean. Ford issued a bulletin for these codes from vacuum leaks.
issues.next: Have a shop do a smoke test to find the leak. It is usually a hose or gasket.

issues.t: Rough idle and stalling at idle
issues.sym: The engine idles rough or unevenly, stalls when coming to a stop, or makes a hooting noise from the idle air valve when slowing down.
issues.why: Dirty or failing idle air control valves and vacuum leaks are common causes. Ford issued bulletins for rough idle, stalling and noise from the idle air bypass valve.
issues.next: Have the idle air control valve cleaned or replaced and check for vacuum leaks.

issues.t: Timing belt shredding (2.0L)
issues.sym: A slapping or rubbing noise from the front of the engine, or the engine suddenly stopping and not restarting.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for 2.0L Zetec timing belts shredding or hitting the front cover. If the belt breaks, the engine stops and can be damaged inside.
issues.next: Replace the timing belt on schedule, around 120,000 miles, or sooner if you do not know when it was last done. Have any noise from the belt area checked right away.

issues.t: Hard starting in freezing weather (2.0L)
issues.sym: Long cranking, a hard start, stalling or rough idle when the engine is cold, especially below freezing.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for 2.0L Zetec cars that over-fuel and start hard in cold weather, fixed with updated engine software or parts.
issues.next: Have the engine checked for codes and ask about the cold-start bulletins.

issues.t: Will not crank in Park but starts in Neutral
issues.sym: Turning the key in Park does nothing, but the car starts if you shift to Neutral.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for the CD4E automatic with this condition. A misadjusted or worn transmission range switch is a common cause.
issues.next: Have the transmission range switch and shift linkage checked. Starting in Neutral is a workaround, but get it fixed.

issues.t: Harsh shifts between gears
issues.sym: A hard bang on the 1-3 upshift or the 3-2 downshift.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for harsh shifts on the CD4E automatic.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Have a shop scan for codes and look at the bulletin fix before the transmission wears further.

issues.t: Manual transmission differential failure (V6)
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the transmission, then the car will not move even though the engine runs.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins about differential failures in the 5-speed manual on V6 cars, sometimes linked to hard launches.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear grinding from the transmission. A used transmission or a rebuild is usually needed.

issues.t: Alternator failure and dead battery
issues.sym: The battery light flickers or stays on, the battery keeps going dead, or the car will not start.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for failed alternators, including corroded slip rings, and for discharged batteries on these cars.
issues.next: Have the battery and alternator tested. Replace the alternator if it is not charging.

issues.t: Starter grinding when starting
issues.sym: A grinding noise when you start the car, or the starter spins without turning the engine.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for starter grinding and poor engagement on these cars.
issues.next: Have the starter and its mounting checked. A worn starter usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Heater core leak
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell inside, foggy windows, a wet passenger floor, or coolant slowly disappearing.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for heater core leaks on these cars. The heater core is behind the dashboard.
issues.next: Check the coolant level and look for wet carpet. Replacing the core is a big job because much of the dash comes out.

issues.t: Heat and A/C blow only from the defrost vents
issues.sym: Air only comes out of the windshield vents no matter which setting you pick.
issues.why: The vent doors are moved by vacuum. A leaking vacuum line or a link falling off a vacuum motor sends all the air to defrost. Ford issued bulletins for both.
issues.next: Have a shop check the vacuum lines and vent door motors behind the dash.

issues.t: Steering wheel shakes when braking
issues.sym: The steering wheel or car vibrates when you brake, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins about brake vibration on these cars, usually from uneven front rotors and pad material.
issues.next: Have the front rotors and pads inspected. New or resurfaced rotors and pads usually fix it.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing noise
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that grows with speed and may change when turning.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for front wheel bearing noise on these cars.
issues.next: Have the wheel bearings checked. A badly worn bearing can affect steering and braking.

issues.t: Clunk from the front stabilizer bar links
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the front when driving over bumps.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for front suspension noise from the stabilizer bar and its links.
issues.next: Have the front sway bar links and bushings checked. They are quick to replace.

issues.t: Dashboard top lifting away from the windshield
issues.sym: The top of the dash curls up near the windshield, exposing the clips underneath and blocking the defroster.
issues.why: The dash top pulls loose over time, especially after hot summers. Owners report it around 47,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Have a shop or trim specialist re-secure the dash. Keep the windshield clear in winter, since the defroster may not work well.

issues.t: Water leaking onto the front floor
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the front floor after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for water getting in around the door panel area and wetting the front floor.
issues.next: Have the door water shield and seals checked and resealed. Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Temperature gauge reads high when the engine is not hot
issues.sym: The temperature gauge sits higher than normal even though the engine is not overheating.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for temperature gauges reading high at normal operating temperature.
issues.next: Make sure the engine is not really overheating first: check coolant level and the fan. Then have the sensor and gauge checked.
